newsitem.title: TURKEY: SOCCER-FENERBAHCE CHAIRMAN IN DISPUTE OVER TURKEY GOALIE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FENERBAHCE CHAIRMAN IN DISPUTE OVER TURKEY GOALIE.

text.p: A dispute has broken out between Fenerbahce chairman Ali Sen and the Turkish Football Federation after Sen stopped club and national team goalkeeper Rustu Recber from playing for Turkey against Wales.
Sen also expressed confidence on Thursday about his club's bid for the European Cup.

Recber, widely recognised as Turkey's best goalie, is to fly to the United States for a miniscus operation on December 12 and will miss the World Cup European group seven match against Wales on December 14.

"The reason is clear. After being operated on the 12th (the doctor) has given me until December 27 for him to be able to play...The league matches in the first six weeks (of the new year) will be the ones that decide the championship," Sen said.
But the Hurriyet newspaper reported that the American doctor due to operate on Recber said there was no medical reason for the operation not to be postponed.
"It is said Rustu has been playing for two years injured. Playing against Wales would only delay him by four days," national coach Mustafa Denizli told the newspaper.
Recber said that the date of his operation was up to the club's board of directors. "I must go along with that," he said.
Meanwhile, Sen is confident his team will qualify for the quarter-finals of the European Cup next Wednesday.
"We will beat Juventus on Wednesday night and Rapid Vienna will beat Manchester United," he said.
Fenerbahce are second in Group C of the Champions' League, one point ahead of Manchester United. The result of Wednesday's games decides which two teams qualify for the quarter-finals.
Sen told reporters that they would then definitely eliminate Porto in the quarter-finals of the European Cup.
"I can't say anything about the semi-final right now. Who knows, but if we get Dortmund, we'll play Juventus in the final," he said.
